model: Normalised underlying-earnings owner-FCF DCF for a multi-affiliate fund manager (equity-accounted associate profit grossed into the earnings base; engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026 economic earnings base, pre-SBC, unlevered, post-tax, in A$m: management Underlying NPAT 138.0 (statutory 176.7 less 52.3 non-cash PAM step-acquisition gain, plus 6.1 one-off transaction costs, plus 7.5 net Principal Investment loss after all CBA interest and interest income) + 6.745 SBC (grossed up so the engine charges it explicitly) - 5.6 performance-fee normalisation (FY26 post-tax perf-fee share 35.6 taken to ~30, the mid-point of a through-cycle 25-35 range on A$61.3bn perf-fee-eligible FUM; FY25's 46.6 was an exceptional Hyperion year). It is NOT statutory revenue (109.7): Pinnacle books its share of 19 Affiliates' post-tax profit (136.0) below its own thin fee line, so revenue x margin is meaningless here and gross profit/EBITDA were deliberately left blank by the parser.
inputs.share_count_basis: 233.112m fully paid shares at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 16(a); the 240.985m register count at 3 July 2026 includes ~7.87m employee loan shares carried as treasury stock, of which only the in-the-money portion dilutes) + 1.744m treasury-stock-method dilution (1.296m loan shares + 0.447m options, note 5(d)) + 2.028m scrip to be issued for AVI (note 31, agreed 4 Aug 2026). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. The 10.547m PAM consideration shares (A$15.97, 24 Apr 2026) are genuine non-SBC issuance and are already in the 30 June count.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: Cash basis: OperatingCashFlowExSeed 113.066 (statutory OCF 348.343 less +235.277 net seed divestment, both KPIs) less capex 5.814 (PPE 0.672 + intangibles 5.142). Statutory FCF of 342.5 is seed-capital timing, not earnings: FY25 was -145.5 on the same definition.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR statement of changes in equity line 3591, 'Share-based payments 17(a) 6,745' ($'000), equals the LTI expense of $6.7m in the results commentary; EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0 every year (loan-share plans, no net-share settlement)
inputs.buyback_note: Pinnacle has never repurchased shares (ShareRepurchases 0 FY16-FY26); the flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company is funding. DRP issued 0.34m shares in FY26.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built. Risk-free 4.4% (Australian 10-yr CGB, Sep-2026), ERP 5.5%, equity beta 1.3 (listed asset managers carry market-plus beta: FUM, base fees and performance fees are all pro-cyclical) -> cost of equity 11.5%. Debt ~8% of capital (A$252m CBA facility vs ~A$3.1bn market cap) at ~6.3% pre-tax / ~4.4% after tax -> WACC 10.9%, rounded to 11.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality and perf-fee volatility are charged in the bear flows, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: occupancy (ROU depreciation + lease interest) is inside Underlying NPAT, so lease liabilities of A$18.5m (2.368 current + 16.149 non-current, FY26 AR note 12) are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt is the CBA facility only (250.0 + 1.868 other).
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: Underlying NPAT 138.0 is attributable to ordinary owners (note 5, profit used for EPS 176,712 is attributable). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.tax_treatment: cash_tax_rate 0% throughout because the earnings base is already post-tax: Affiliate profit arrives as a post-tax equity-accounted share, and Pinnacle's own income tax (A$9.9m FY26) on its contract revenue is inside Underlying NPAT.
inputs.interest_treatment: Management's Underlying NPAT excludes the ENTIRE Principal Investment return net of CBA interest expense (7.9) and interest income (2.2) (results commentary p.22-23: 'net overall return on PI, net of the interest expense on the CBA loan and interest income, was a loss of $7.5 million'). The flows are therefore unlevered and ex-interest-income; the matching assets (PI book at fair value, cash) sit in the bridge and the CBA debt is deducted as net debt. interest_income 2.22 is recorded for the cash-basis owner FCF (last_fcf) reconstruction only.
inputs.reinvestment_note: capex_pct_path is NOT PPE capex (A$0.7m). It is the reinvestment the growth needs: Pinnacle-level seed capital / equity recycling / new-affiliate stakes plus the share of Affiliate profit the Affiliates retain rather than distribute (FY26 dividends received from Affiliates A$109.3m vs profit share A$136.0m = 80%; owner cash FCF / underlying NPAT ran 78% FY24, 96% FY25, 71% FY26, ~82% average). 13% of the base in FY27 tapering to 5% by FY36 gives year-1 owner FCF at ~86% of the post-SBC earnings base, matching history, and lets conversion rise as the affiliate stable matures.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (a1),(b),(c),(d),(f)) run through the Drivers/engine route with the 'revenue' driver redefined as a normalised underlying-earnings base. Pinnacle is an operating company whose value is a stream of distributable profit, not a bank, REIT or LIC, so the non-FCF models do not fit; but the engine's revenue x EBITDA-margin build cannot be applied to its P&L because (1) equity-accounted Affiliate profit (A$136.0m) is post-tax and below the A$109.7m revenue line, so net income is 1.6x revenue; (2) statutory OCF is dominated by seed-capital flows (-145 FY25, +348 FY26). Hence: base = Underlying NPAT ex step-gain, ex PI, ex interest, + SBC gross-up, - perf-fee normalisation; ebitda_margin 100%; cash tax 0%; explicit reinvestment charge; PI book (+198.8) and post-balance-date deal costs (Metrics -100.5, AVI -44.9) in the equity bridge; CBA debt less cash as net debt. Risk is charged once: in the bear flows and a market-beta WACC, never both. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical asset manager; Gordon at 11%/3% is 12.9x so the cap does not bind in base). No formal guidance: Pinnacle does not forecast markets; FY27 base growth is built bottom-up from the acquired uplift (full-year 100% PAM: FY26 carried ~2 months consolidated + 10 months at 24.9%; Metrics stake 28.4% -> ~35% from 23 Jul 2026; AVI) plus modest organic growth on opening FUM 28% above FY26's opening. Price is intraday; refresh at the next regular close.
inputs.pi_book_note: Financial assets at FVTPL 196.521 current + 2.240 non-current (FY26 AR note 8(a), 30 Jun 2026; 188.5 held in Affiliate-managed strategies, partially hedged). The 81.7 Advantage Partners stake at FVOCI is NOT in the bridge: its dividends (2.1) flow through revenue and are inside the earnings base (matching-asset rule).

equity_bridge.item: Principal Investments (seed book) at fair value, 30 Jun 2026
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 8(a): FVTPL 196.521 current + 2.240 non-current. Its returns (and the CBA interest that funds it) are excluded from Underlying NPAT, so the asset is added at value. Management's own 'cash and PI net of CBA debt' was A$36.0m = 89.5 + 198.8 - 251.9 - 0.4 rounding.

equity_bridge.item: Metrics Credit Holdings +6.8% stake, completed 23 Jul 2026
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 31: ~A$100.5m, 75% on completion, 25% twelve months from agreement. Restores Pinnacle's Metrics interest from 28.37% to ~35%; the earnings uplift is in the FY27 growth rate, so the cost is deducted here.

equity_bridge.item: AVI cash consideration (via PAM), agreed 4 Aug 2026
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 31: ~A$25.3m cash on completion + £10.2m (~A$19.6m) cash 12 months after completion; the ~A$31.9m scrip component is 2.028m shares already added to the share count. AVI (~£1.9bn FUM) earnings are in the FY27 growth rate.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: 10-year geometric mean of the base-case driver path (24% FY27 acquired-uplift year decaying to 3.5% by FY36); historical CAGRs are all inflated by acquisitions and the FY25 A$441.8m raise and none is a usable forward anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 36.5% exceeds diluted-EPS 5-yr CAGR 16.4% by >30%: book value was inflated by the FY25 A$441.8m placement/SPP and the FY26 A$168.3m PAM scrip issue, not by retained earnings (Pinnacle pays out ~100% of underlying NPAT). Equity CAGR is not the growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs (34.1%/27.5%) are on Pinnacle's own contract revenue (FY23 45.5 -> FY26 109.7; FY21 32.5), boosted by PAM consolidation from Apr-2026 and are not the earnings base. EPS CAGRs are on diluted statutory EPS (FY21 0.365, FY23 0.390, FY26 0.781); FY26 includes the 52.3 step-gain, on underlying EPS (FY25 0.53 -> FY26 0.61) growth was 15%. FCF CAGRs are on the owner cash series (OCF ex seed - capex - SBC - interest income: FY21 54.46, FY23 56.93, FY26 98.29). The reported FCF series (FY21 32.9 -> FY26 342.5) is seed-capital timing and has no CAGR meaning. Owner cash FCF has compounded at 12.5% over 5 years against 27%+ for underlying NPAT: an increasing share of the profit growth is being retained inside the Affiliates or recycled into seed and stakes, which is why the model carries an explicit reinvestment charge. Underlying NPAT FY16 5.8 -> FY26 138.0 is a 37.3% 10-yr CAGR.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +24%: ~+20pp acquired (full-year 100% PAM vs FY26's ~2 months consolidated + 10 months at 24.9%, on a business bought for A$397m/75.1% -> ~A$17m uplift; Metrics 28.4%->~35% from 23 Jul 2026 -> ~A$10m; AVI ~A$3m) net of integration cost, plus ~+4pp organic: base fees up on opening FUM 28% higher, largely offset by Affiliate expense growth (FY26 expenses ran ~22% above consensus), Horizon 2/3 investment and the perf-fee normalisation already in the base. FY28-FY36 decays 10% -> 3.5%: existing-affiliate FUM compounding plus new Horizon 2 affiliates, at roughly a third of the 28% 10-yr FUM CAGR because market beta (11.8bn of FY26's 50bn FUM increase) is not assumed to repeat and profit share (~37%) trails FUM share (~40%).

scenario_narratives.base: The acquired uplift lands in FY27 (full-year PAM at 100%, Metrics back to ~35%, AVI folded into PAM) and organic growth is modest as Affiliate expense growth and Horizon 2/3 spend absorb most of the base-fee gain from a 28% higher opening FUM. Performance fees run at a through-cycle ~A$30m post-tax, not FY25's A$46.6m. From FY28 the platform compounds at 10% decaying to 3.5% on existing-affiliate flows (private markets and international distribution growing faster than domestic public equities) with reinvestment tapering from 13% to 5% of earnings as the affiliate stable matures and distributes more. Gordon binds the terminal value (12.9x owner FCF, under the 15x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: PAM/AVI make Pinnacle a genuine global distribution platform: international FUM (33% of total) keeps compounding, Horizon 2 adds two or three new affiliates on the 2018-2021 pattern, private credit (Metrics) and private markets (Five V, Advantage option to 13%) stay in structural demand, and Affiliate profit share catches up with FUM share as FY26's incentive-cost step-up normalises. Perf-fee-eligible FUM (A$61bn, 34% 10-yr CAGR) delivers above-normal fees in strong markets. FY27 +30%, then 15% decaying to 5%, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY27 still carries the acquired uplift (+14%) but FY28 brings the market dislocation management keeps warning about: a 15% FUM drawdown, performance fees near zero, net outflows in retail and the private-equity exit freeze hitting Five V and Advantage fundraising, while Affiliate cost bases (performance-linked incentives, PAM/AVI integration, compliance across five jurisdictions) do not flex down, so earnings fall 15% then a further 3% before recovering at 8% decaying to 2.5%. SBC rises to 5.2% of a smaller base. The A$250m CBA facility, drawn against a mark-to-market seed book, is a solvency non-issue but limits new-affiliate firepower. Terminal growth 2.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: FUM, base fees, performance fees, seed-book marks and net flows are all pro-cyclical and management says so; the FY26 result showed Affiliate costs growing faster than revenue and profit share trailing FUM share; and key-person/minority-stake risk sits outside Pinnacle's control. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once: strong markets, perf fees above normal, PAM/AVI integration working, and the profit-share gap closing. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Pinnacle is valued as an operating company: an owner-FCF DCF, because its value is a growing stream of distributable profit from 19 Affiliates plus its own distribution/RE fees. The dcf-methods non-FCF routes were considered and rejected: it is not a bank (no deposits), not a REIT (no AFFO), not a LIC or holdco (it does not sit on a portfolio at NAV; the Affiliate stakes are equity-accounted operating interests carried at A$0.2bn against an earnings stream worth billions, so NTA is meaningless), and there is no live corporate action. What has to change is the engine's inputs, not the engine: the P&L structure (post-tax Affiliate profit share below a thin revenue line; net income 1.6x revenue) and the seed-capital noise in OCF make revenue x margin and statutory FCF both unusable, so the 'revenue' driver is a normalised Underlying NPAT base (ex PAM step-gain, ex Principal Investment returns and all interest, perf fees normalised to ~A$30m, SBC grossed up so the engine charges it), margin 100%, tax 0% (already post-tax), and an explicit reinvestment charge (13% -> 5% of earnings) standing in for seed capital, equity recycling and Affiliate profit retention (dividends received were 80% of profit share in FY26). Every income stream stripped has its asset in the bridge (PI book at fair value +A$198.8m) and the debt that funds it is net debt (A$162.4m); post-balance-date deal costs (Metrics -A$100.5m, AVI -A$44.9m) are deducted because their earnings are in the FY27 growth rate. WACC 11% in AUD, the same in all scenarios; risk is charged in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not in the rate. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF for a cyclical asset manager. On these assumptions the stock, even after a 39% drawdown from the 52-week high, sits above the probability-weighted value; the required-return table shows what discount rate today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Performance-fee normalisation level: every A$10m of post-tax perf fees is ~7% of the earnings base; FY25 46.6 / FY26 35.6 against an assumed ~30 through-cycle

Reinvestment charge (13% -> 5%): if Affiliates keep retaining ~20% of profit and Pinnacle keeps seeding at FY22/FY25 scale, owner FCF conversion stays near 80% and the taper is too generous; if retention is timing, the model is too harsh by ~A$1/share

FY27 acquired uplift (~+20pp): PAM's earnings power is inferred from the A$397m/75.1% price and 2 months of consolidated revenue, not disclosed; Metrics' contribution is inferred from the A$100.5m/6.8% price
Market beta: 11.8bn of FY26's 50bn FUM increase was market movement; a bear-style drawdown in FY27 rather than FY28 removes the acquired uplift's cushion
Affiliate cost capture: FY26 Affiliate expenses ran ~22% above consensus and Pinnacle's profit share (~37%) trails its FUM share (~40%); the model assumes no further slippage
Share count: 7.9m employee loan shares sit outside the 233.1m issued count and only 1.3m are counted as dilutive; a sustained re-rating would bring more into the money
Currency: PAM/AVI (GBP), VSS (USD), Advantage (JPY), Langdon (CAD) earnings are now material and the AUD base carries translation risk not modelled
